text.p: 1415 GMT - Swiss shares closed slightly weaker but above the day's lows after a steady decline throughout most of the session.

Dealers said attention in an otherwise slow market concentrated on pharmaceuticals. Roche will release its figures for the first half-year on Tuesday. Results of Ciba and Sandoz, which plan to merge into Novartis, will follow on Wednesday.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was down 10.7 points, or 0.29 percent, at 3,714.7 points.
* The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 5.70 points, or 0.24 percent, to 2,376.50 points.

Dealers said volumes were generally low. The market's sluggishness stemmed from banking holiday in London and investors' reluctance to build up positions ahead of numerous half-year figures during this week, one trader noted.
Apart from the big three pharmaceuticals, Alusuisse, Swissair and Oerlikon Buehrle should release figures this week.

* Sandoz added one franc to 1,465 francs. The company today announced the sale of its Master Builders Technologies (MBT) to Viag's SKW Trostberg for 1.3 billion francs. One analyst considered this an "excellent deal".
* Ciba registered shares fell five francs to 1,558.

Analysts on average expect Roche to report an rise in first half net profit of 17.3 percent to 2.24 billion Swiss francs compared with an expected rise of 14.5 percent at Sandoz to 1.26 billion and an 11.3 percent rise at Ciba to 1.67 billion.
* EMS-Chemie, trading ex-dividend of 150 francs, closed 30 francs lower at 5,010.
* Banks and insurers were mixed. UBS slid five francs to 1,196, while CS Holding advanced 0.50 francs to 128.25.
* Swiss Re advanced five francs to 1,270 francs. Winterthur put on one franc to 757, while Zurich gave up one franc to 330.

Swiss Re which had been rumoured to be interested in purchasing the Mercantile & General (M&G) reinsurance unit of Prudential Corp., restated that it would not comment on such rumours. However, the company added there would be clarity over the situation in a few days.
